paragraphs: Friend, here's what Moses is getting at in Deuteronomy 6. God doesn't want a little corner of your life. He wants all of it: "all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength" (Deuteronomy 6:5). The LORD is One (Deuteronomy 6:4), so there's no second spot on the shelf for anybody else.

Now, loving God with all of you is not a Sunday-only thing. Moses says to teach these words to your children, and to speak of them at home, on the road, when you lie down and when you get up (Deuteronomy 6:7). The whole day, baker! That tells me love for God is meant to soak into ordinary life, like vanilla into dough.

And here's the part that sneaks up on you. The good stuff comes, the cities, the wells, the full belly, and that's when Moses says to be careful not to forget the LORD (Deuteronomy 6:10-12). I know a little about being rescued and then getting comfortable, and comfort makes memory fuzzy. So keep the story of what God has done where you can see it, and let it shape how you love Him today.
